_comment: ICAO type designators and operator-name keywords used by adsb_classify.
Edit freely — the classifier reloads this file when its mtime changes, so
you can add a type without restarting.
Three tiers, because 'military' and 'interesting to see' are not
military  — in service with an air arm somewhere. Strong signal.
warbird   — ex-military airframe now on a civil register. This is what
actually flies over the Gold Coast: L-39s, Jet Provosts,
aerobatic — purpose-built display types. Weak on their own (a Pitts
doing weekend circuits is not news); meaningful when they
turn up low inside an anon_signal zone or with a display operator.
Type codes are matched exactly against the feed's 't' field, uppercased.
_military_note: Only types that are essentially NEVER civil belong here. Anything with a
large civil fleet must come out, however often an air force also flies it:
the multi-signal design already catches those via hex block, dbFlags or
callsign prefix, so listing them here buys nothing and costs false
positives. Learned the hard way — an early version listed A332 for the
RAAF KC-30A and promptly flagged a Qantas A330, a China Eastern A330 and
a maintenance ferry. Same for BE20 (King Air), CL60 (Challenger), FA7X
and GLF5: the RAAF examples all carry ADF hex addresses anyway.

_comment: Emergency-service and government aircraft. Not military, and not a
confidence signal - they get their own 'special' role, which airspace
zones can alert on. Operator keywords are substrings of the feed's
ownOp field; ident prefixes are exact prefixes of the ADS-B callsign.
A starting list - extend it with what you actually see locally.
